plan.headline: Meridian Home Goods: 48 entries reviewed, and 7 (about $21,024.00) have deadlines within days. Start with those.

steps.title: Act today on 3 entries due Oct 24, 2026
steps.detail: These results are as of Oct 24, 2026, so call your broker right away to confirm these can still be filed. One goes in CAPE (CBP's refund portal for IEEPA duties). The other two need a protest (a formal request to CBP to correct an entry).

steps.title: File 2 CAPE claims due Oct 25, 2026
steps.detail: These entries appear eligible for CAPE and the deadline is the next day.

steps.title: File a protest by Oct 26, 2026
steps.detail: CAPE will reject this entry because it was liquidated (CBP's final calculation of duties) more than 80 days ago. It is still inside the 180-day protest window.

steps.title: File a protest by Oct 30, 2026
steps.detail: This entry is past CAPE's 80-day limit but still inside the protest window.

steps.title: File 4 more protests between Nov 6 and Nov 26, 2026
steps.detail: These are all past CAPE's 80-day limit but still inside the protest window. The first deadline is Nov 6, 2026.

steps.title: Withdraw one protest, then file in CAPE by Dec 3, 2026
steps.detail: This entry's protest was filed only for the IEEPA refund. It can be withdrawn so the entry can go into CAPE while it is still within 80 days of liquidation.

steps.title: Fix one entry, then file in CAPE by Dec 10, 2026
steps.detail: A goods value is reported on a Chapter 99 line, and CAPE rejects the entry until your broker moves it to the Chapter 1-97 line.

steps.title: File in CAPE by Dec 23, 2026
steps.detail: This entry appears eligible for CAPE now.

steps.title: File a protest by Dec 24, 2026
steps.detail: This entry is past CAPE's 80-day limit but still inside the protest window.

steps.title: File 5 protests between Jan 9 and Jan 31, 2027
steps.detail: These are past CAPE's 80-day limit but still inside the protest window. Your broker can file them with the earlier protests.

steps.title: File 2 CAPE claims by Jan 10 and Jan 11, 2027
steps.detail: These entries appear eligible for CAPE. Filing them early with your other CAPE claims is simpler.

steps.title: File 7 more CAPE claims with no deadline given
steps.detail: These appear eligible for CAPE now. Your CAPE file lists 14 entries worth $58,592.50 in total, including the CAPE entries above.

steps.title: File one entry in CAPE Phase 2
steps.detail: This entry is flagged for reconciliation (a later duty adjustment) with no type 09 filed yet. It appears covered by CAPE Phase 2, open since Jun 29, 2026.

steps.title: Talk to your broker about 4 entries that don't fit CAPE
steps.detail: Two may be AD/CVD, warehouse, bonded or reconciliation entries, so ask how CBP is treating them. One was paid by a surety (a bond company), and CBP says not to file those in CAPE. One is tied to a drawback claim, which is excluded from CAPE. Together these four are $19,795.50.

steps.title: Leave one open protest where it is
steps.detail: A protest is already open and the entry is past 80 days. It stays on the protest route, and CAPE rejects entries with an open protest.

steps.title: Wait on 7 finally liquidated entries (court class action)
steps.detail: These entries can't use CAPE or a protest. A court certified a class of importers who haven't sued (Freestyle World, Oct 8, 2026), but there is no refund order yet. The class may not cover goods from Brazil or India. For a large balance, ask a customs attorney about your own suit. These total $16,143.50, and MH3-2526883-7's amount comes from a statement only, so have your broker check it.

steps.title: Nothing to do on 6 entries
steps.detail: No IEEPA duty was paid on these, so there's nothing to refund. Section 301 and 232 duties aren't part of this refund. This is not legal advice, and entries only "appear eligible", so confirm everything with your broker.

Thanks,
Meridian Home Goods Co.

checker.summary: I compared the 48 extracted entries against the 47 CBP 7501 pages and the 2-page broker statement. All 48 entry numbers are present. For the entries with 7501 pages, the IEEPA line items sum to the statement totals. The Section 301 and 232 labels (9903.88.03, 9903.81.91, 9903.85.08) look correct. The surety-paid, open-protest (IEEPA only), drawback and reconciliation flags are supported by the statement and 7501s. I found four issues. (1) MH3-6191079-5 is extracted as liquidation 'unknown', but the statement shows it liquidated 04/01/2026, and its own note says liquidation is suspended. (2) That same entry therefore carries a conflict inside the statement that should be surfaced. (3) MH3-9692647-6 is a type 21 warehouse entry with no warehouse flag. (4) MH3-2526883-7 has no 7501, so its IEEPA figure of 3280 comes from the statement only and can't be checked against line detail. One further oddity: MH3-8628656-4 shows a liquidation date of 10/23/2026, which is after the statement's 10/22/2026 prepared date. The extraction matches the statement on this, so I did not list it as an issue.
